title: How society shapes and reads science
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point covers how people can read the same evidence differently or share only suitable data; the closest points only cover how funding and ethics steer which research goes ahead.

draft.title: How society shapes and reads science
card: People and groups can read the same evidence in different ways. They may weigh it differently because of their values, their needs or what they have to gain or lose.
Some people or groups share only the data that suits them. This leaves out evidence that points the other way and gives a one-sided picture.
Society's values and needs also affect which research gets funded. Money often goes to problems that people, governments or companies see as important.
Checking where evidence comes from, and whether all the data is shown, helps a reader judge a claim.
draft.remember: Evidence can be read in different ways or shared in part, and society's needs affect what research is funded.

a.q: A company shares only the trials in which its sunscreen worked well and leaves out two trials in which it did not. What is this an example of?
opts: Sharing only the data that suits the company
Funding research according to society's needs
Two groups reading the same evidence differently
A result that other teams have repeated
a.why: The company left out data that pointed the other way, so the picture is one-sided. This is different from two groups reading the same full evidence differently, because here the evidence itself was cut down.
a.clue: Look at what was left out.

b.q: A state government sees rising rates of a disease in its towns and puts more money into research on that disease. Which idea does this show?
opts: Society's needs affect which research is funded
Groups share only the data that suits them
People read the same evidence in different ways
Funding makes a research result true
b.why: The government responded to a need in its community by funding research on it. Funding shows what society values, but it does not make a result true.
b.clue: Ask why the money was given to this topic.

a.best: Sharing only the data that suits the company

b.best: Society's needs affect which research is funded
